text: ok so look one more time though at like the way you make decals and tell me why this cant be apart of the normal painter
resolution: Read both stacks end-to-end (editors/paint/ layer model + game/textures/decal.ts DecalDoc + the materials compose lens) and answered the question in §12 of the structure review (commit ab7ff87b8): NOTHING structural separates the decal composer from the normal painter — they are the vector half and raster half of one editor, split only by lineage (cutout cart vs /compose route). Both are layer stacks with the same strip verbs, both already have image layers, both exit through Materialize into the same materials store. Proposed the unified model: the paint document's layer gains a kind (mask | text | rect | image), node layers stay parametric with a rasterize verb, the merged doc rides the material losslessly both ways (existing DecalDoc = merged doc with zero mask layers, so migration is trivial). Named the honest costs: the compositor interleave (React-captured node layers z-ordered between GPU paintable mask quads — the real work), a move/select tool in the painter, history unification per V20. The locked shader|decal|image→Materialize vocabulary survives — sources become layer kinds, Materialize stays the one exit.
